$comment: TEMPLATE. The target below is REGISTERED (control-plane identity confirmed) but NOT AUTHORIZED for any hosted operation — every flag is false and each must be raised separately, by a human, for one operation at a time. Copy to ~/aw-r02-evidence/environment-manifest.json. NEVER add a password, service-role key, anon/publishable key, access token, connection string or DSN: scripts/lib/r02TargetGuard.mjs refuses a manifest containing any such key.

environment.name: afterworth-nonprod
environment.purpose: R-02 Model C hosted-compatibility testing only
environment.lifecycle: disposable — expected to be reset repeatedly and possibly deleted after R-02

notes: allowlisted_refs is deliberately redundant with project_ref. The guard requires the target to be BOTH named and allowlisted, so a ref pasted into project_ref by accident does not become authorized.
One flag per operation, never a shared 'mutation' flag: authorizing a bootstrap must not incidentally authorize a reset, a metadata write, or a deploy.

Registration is CONTROL-PLANE identity. It proves which Supabase project was created. It does NOT prove that a database session connects to that project under the expected execution identity — that is R02_2 and needs its own authorization.

hosted_sql_read_authorized was raised to true for qxzeougbaarecaiiqsay ONLY, and ONLY for the SELECT-only capability pack. Every other flag stays false: authorizing a read must not drift into authorizing a write. See HOSTED_READ_AUTHORIZATION in scripts/lib/r02TargetGuard.mjs for the reviewable grant.

mutation_test_authorized gates the isolated event-trigger probe and is FALSE. It is a separate flag from bootstrap_authorized on purpose: the probe answers one narrow privilege question and must not be reachable through a bootstrap approval. expected_model.probe_version pins WHICH reviewed probe an authorization covers, so editing the probe cannot inherit an old approval.

mutation_test_authorized was raised to true for qxzeougbaarecaiiqsay ONLY, for event_trigger_probe ONLY, at probe_version v1 ONLY. Every other flag stays false. See MUTATION_TEST_AUTHORIZATION in scripts/lib/r02TargetGuard.mjs, which also pins the probe SQL SHA-256 so an edited probe cannot inherit this approval.

mutation_test_authorized was returned to FALSE after probe v1 was executed and cleaned. The grant is marked consumed in MUTATION_TEST_AUTHORIZATION, and the guard refuses a consumed probe even if the flag were set true again - a one-question authorization must not become a standing mutation licence.

bootstrap_manifest_sha256 pins the cumulative hash of all 13 bootstrap phase files. MODEL_C_BOOTSTRAP_0060 is authorized by HASH, not by verb inspection: one substituted statement in 921 would pass any plausible allowlist.
model_c_bootstrap_0060_authorized is DISTINCT from bootstrap_authorized. A broad bootstrap approval must not silently authorize this specific hash-pinned 921-statement run.

model_c_bootstrap_0060_authorized was raised to true for qxzeougbaarecaiiqsay ONLY, VERSION 0060 ONLY, manifest hash 69ec3a15...ad67 ONLY. It authorizes applying the bootstrap; it does NOT authorize recovery, reset, migration metadata writes, or deployment. A phase failing after mutation means PARTIAL_BOOTSTRAP and a stop, not an undo.
